standard_prerequisites.name: A pseudo-coherent complex is represented by a bounded above complex of finite free modules, and a finite module over a local ring that is generated by its reduction can be generated by lifts modulo an arbitrarily high power of the maximal ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies the choice of the elements y_b and the localization that makes the three listed conditions hold.

standard_prerequisites.name: If a map of finite free modules has a surjective reduction modulo a prime and its cokernel becomes finite projective after inverting some element outside the prime, then the cokernel itself is finite projective after that localization
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the finite projective quotient E^{i+1} that makes the upper truncation perfect.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a distinguished triangle whose first term has no cohomology above a given degree and whose third term is perfect with amplitude starting at that degree, the triangle splits and exhibits the middle term as a direct sum of the two truncations
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the displayed canonical isomorphism and finishes the proof.

core_obligations: Reduce to a bounded above complex of finite free modules, fix notation with tensor products over the ring and write kappa for the residue field at the given prime, then define the subspaces V and W of the fibre of the i-th term as the image of the previous differential and the kernel of the next one, with dimensions r, s and t (proof lines 19765-19785).

Choose elements x_1, ..., x_r in degree i-1 mapping to a basis of V, elements y_1, ..., y_s in the kernel of the i-th differential mapping to a basis of the quotient W over V, using the surjectivity hypothesis, and elements z_1, ..., z_t mapping to a basis of the quotient of the fibre by W; observe that the images of the z_c in the next term are linearly independent in the fibre (proof lines 19786-19792).

Apply the cokernel statement to localize at an element outside the prime so that three conditions hold: the elements d^i(x_a), y_b, z_c form a basis of the i-th term, the images d^i(z_c) are linearly independent in the next term, and the quotient of the next term by the span of those images is finite projective (proof lines 19793-19800).

Use that the differential annihilates the images of the x_a and the y_b, together with the linear independence of the d^i(z_c), to identify that quotient with the cokernel of the i-th differential, so that the upper truncation is a bounded complex of finite projective modules sitting in the degrees from i+1 up (proof lines 19801-19809).

Apply the splitting statement to the distinguished triangle of the two truncations, whose lower part has no cohomology above degree i and whose upper part is perfect with amplitude starting at i+1, to obtain the displayed canonical isomorphism in the derived category of the localization (proof lines 19810-19818).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a bounded above complex of finite free modules and describe the fibre in the critical degree by the two subspaces V and W (proof lines 19765-19785).
Lift bases of V, of W over V and of the fibre over W to elements of the complex, using the surjectivity hypothesis for the middle family (proof lines 19786-19792).
Localize outside the prime so that the lifted elements form a basis and the quotient by the images of the third family is finite projective (proof lines 19793-19800).
Identify the upper truncation with a bounded complex of finite projective modules and apply the splitting statement to the triangle of truncations (proof lines 19801-19818).
difficulty_reason: The statement is a local splitting result for a pseudo-coherent complex: if at a prime the natural map from the cohomology to the cohomology of the derived fibre is surjective in some degree, then after inverting one element outside the prime the upper truncation becomes perfect with amplitude starting at that degree and the complex splits as the direct sum of its two truncations (statement lines 19743-19763). The proof analyses the fibre in the critical degree through the image and kernel subspaces, lifts bases of the three pieces, and uses the surjectivity hypothesis precisely to lift the middle family, after which a localization makes the lifted elements a basis and the relevant quotient finite projective, so that the splitting statement can be applied (proof lines 19765-19818). The degree bookkeeping that identifies the quotient with the cokernel of the differential is what makes the upper truncation perfect.
